Some pretty recent high profile titles. I for one was definitely hoping they would pick up Oregairu as I started reading the Light Novel and would definitely want to buy it.

I think it's great that there'll be a proper release for Baccano!, if any series on this list deserved it, that one does. I've been reading fan translated versions of the novels for a while so it's great that I can officially support the author in some way.

Man, the cheers at the Yen Press panel when they announced Baccanno! That was a big surprise and a very welcome one.

Some additional info on the manga simulpubs that got left out - while they're looking to start their simulpub program in October of 2015, most of the manga listed will be seeing catch-up releases through the summer, so there's that to look forward to.

Further information on print/digital releases:

  1. Handa-Kun will be released digitally in November '15 and in print January '16
  2. Baccano! is looking at an April/March '16 release target
  3. OreGairu (working title "My Youth Romantic Comedy is Wrong as I Expected") is looking at an "early 2016" release

And, since I took notes on it and I've got my newsman hat on already: how exactly does YP choose what novels to adapt? The answer, as given by them, is twofold:

  1. How much of a fanbase is there for this title?
  2. How much do we like the title?

Quote the panel:

You read the material, you see the merit of the title and see if the characters are engaging and if the story flow is strong and if it's not gonna be too hard for the English audience to relate to. All this stuff plays an important role in our decision. It depends title by title whether we think it'd have a strong fanbase in the English market as well.

There was a pretty strong emphasis on the YenPress team trying to reach beyond the established anime/LN fandom that currently exists and reaching further into the Western market as a whole - in other words, make Eastern light novels mainstream in the West. It's a lofty goal to be sure but, given their current lineup of novels and plans for the future regarding accessibility and ease of licensing, it's probably not one too far out of reach. Their partnership with Square Enix sure doesn't hurt.
